name: Zoho CRM
tagline: Manage a focused contact and deal pipeline without recreating the wider Zoho suite

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Maximum 3 users; 10 custom email templates, 10 data exports and 5,000 API calls/day

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 50,000 base API credits/day plus 250 per user (100,000 maximum); 5 Marketplace extensions; multiple pipelines

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: 50,000 base API credits/day plus 500 per user (3,000,000 maximum); 10 Marketplace extensions; unlimited reports

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 50,000 base API credits/day plus 1,000 per user (5,000,000 maximum); 20 Marketplace extensions; territory management and sandbox

tiers.name: Ultimate
tiers.limits: 50,000 base API credits/day plus 2,000 per user with no stated maximum; 50 Marketplace extensions and enhanced limits

pricing.freeTierCaps: 3 users; 10 custom email templates; 10 exports; 5,000 API calls/day
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (up to 34% off); pay-as-you-go with no contract; local taxes extra
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid premium support and implementation/onboarding services are optional extras. Third-party integrations can require separate licenses; extra API/function credits and some mail-merge or messaging capacity are sold as add-ons.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Zoho CRM, manage a focused contact and deal pipeline without recreating the wider Zoho suite. The hard boundary is ecosystem breadth, integrations, automation, analytics, and enterprise controls, plus integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in.
coreLoopDIY: Manage contacts and companies, move deals through a focused pipeline, log interactions, and surface the next action without recreating the wider Zoho suite.
whatYouLose: ecosystem breadth, integrations, automation, analytics, and enterprise controls
moatNotes: integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in
ongoingBurden: deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Zoho CRM because CRM value compounds as the system becomes the shared memory of every customer interaction and embeds itself in the rest of the stack. The recurring cost buys deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Twenty
priorArt.desc: Active open-source modern CRM with extensible data models.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.desc: A traditional CRM that actually lets you change the data model; polished enough, but still your server.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records in MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL; uploaded files on the application server
facts.gapVsPaid: It has a smaller integration, automation, analytics and AI ecosystem than Zoho CRM and makes you administer the deployment.
facts.setupBlocker: A server with PHP and a supported database, or Docker; production also needs HTTPS, mail, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: Frappe CRM
alternatives.desc: A clean leads-and-deals board with notes, tasks and email; Frappe underneath means a real server, not a toy.

facts.install: Frappe Cloud signup, or easy-install script, Bench or Docker
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in the Frappe site database; attachments in the site's file storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is narrower and less mature in workflow automation, reporting, integrations and administration than Zoho CRM.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting means Linux plus Frappe Bench or Docker, database and Redis services, a domain, mail configuration and upgrades

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.dataFormat: Records and files live in HubSpot's cloud; CRM records can be exported as CSV or XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: The free tier gates the customization, workflow automation and reporting depth that a paid Zoho CRM user is likely replacing.

alternatives.name: Krayin CRM
alternatives.desc: A Laravel sales pipeline with leads, contacts and email; glossy enough, but it still wants a PHP stack.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records in MySQL; uploaded files in Laravel application storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It has far fewer integrations, automation options, reports and mobile capabilities than Zoho CRM.
facts.setupBlocker: A PHP, Laravel and MySQL server stack or Docker, followed by web-server, mail, HTTPS and backup configuration

alternatives.name: SuiteCRM
alternatives.desc: The old-school full-fat CRM: every module you remember, plus the server you now own.

facts.install: Download archive and run the web installer on a LAMP or LEMP stack
facts.dataFormat: CRM data in MySQL or MariaDB; uploaded files on the application server
facts.gapVsPaid: Its interface and administration feel dated beside Zoho CRM, and its integrations, mobile experience and AI features are less turnkey.
facts.setupBlocker: A supported PHP, web-server and database stack, correct file permissions, cron, mail and ongoing patching

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.dataFormat: CRM data in PostgreSQL, jobs and cache in Redis, and files in local or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is newer and substantially less broad in mature modules, automation, reporting and integrations than Zoho CRM.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker Compose, environment variables, a domain, email, persistent storage, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: Odoo CRM One App Free
alternatives.desc: A full hosted pipeline for unlimited users, provided CRM is the only Odoo app you marry.

facts.dataFormat: CRM data and attachments live in Odoo Online's managed database and filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a capable pipeline, but the one-app-free rule and weaker sales-specific ecosystem make it a poor substitute for Zoho's wider CRM workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: None for CRM alone; installing a second Odoo app ends the one-app-free arrangement

alternatives.name: Freshsales Free
alternatives.desc: A clean three-user pipeline with email and mobile apps; useful automation starts asking for rent.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records and files live in Freshworks' cloud; contacts and deals can be imported or exported by CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Its free tier has less workflow, reporting, customization and ecosystem depth than paid Zoho CRM.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Standard plan and a personal or very small-team CRM DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Zoho CRM in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage contacts and companies, move deals through a focused pipeline, log interactions, and surface the next action without recreating the wider Zoho suite.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, opportunities, notes, tasks, and configurable pipeline stages.
Add fast global search, duplicate detection, merge, CSV import, and CSV export.
Provide a chronological interaction timeline with manual email and meeting logging.
Implement saved views, filters, owner assignment, and a next-action dashboard.
Add role-based access, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out automatic mailbox ingestion.
Deliberately leave out commercial enrichment databases.
Deliberately leave out enterprise forecasting, integrations, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
